title: Repository Tool Lifecycle path-filter and branch-literal boundary

phases.objective: Keep permanent workflow branch-literal enforcement fail-closed while preventing repository path filters from being misclassified as work-branch names.

e2e_journeys.terminal_outcome: The lifecycle guard ignores only nested paths and paths-ignore values, continues to reject actual branch and git-push literals, and emits no false finding for valid repository path filters.
steps: Load the repository maintenance policy and canonical lifecycle guard.
Evaluate a workflow that declares a real gpt work branch and prove BRANCH_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW remains reported.
Evaluate a workflow containing a git push to a work branch and prove repository-mutation safeguards remain active.
Evaluate read-only pull-request paths containing docs/work-maps and feat/example repository paths.
Prove nested paths and paths-ignore values are excluded from branch-literal classification without excluding sibling workflow keys.
Run the full repository lifecycle regression suite and require every governance assertion to pass.
assertions: Actual branch declarations and script-level work-branch literals remain detectable.
Only nested values under paths and paths-ignore are excluded from branch-literal scanning.
Repository path filters do not produce BRANCH_SPECIFIC_WORKFLOW findings.
No repository mutation, workflow dispatch, credential access, provider call, migration, deployment, main write, or Production write occurs.

phases.objective: This repository-governance correction performs no runtime, migration, database, provider, deployment, main, or Production operation.
